name: Kawa-no-Kami
description: Kawa-no-Kami is the generic Shinto designation for a river deity in Japanese mythology — the spirit or god (kami) of a river, sometimes treated as a single 'king of the river gods' and at other times as a class of localized spirits resident in specific rivers.

aliases.name: Kahaku
aliases.meaning: river earl / river lord (河伯), borrowed from Chinese Hebo

aliases.name: Suijin
aliases.meaning: water deity (broader category encompassing river kami)

origin: Throughout the Japanese archipelago wherever rivers are venerated; the figure is part of the broader East Asian river-deity complex (Chinese Hebo, Korean Habaek).
